facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 金_偏财 (Metal carrying The Horizon). Persona The Horizon (偏财). Definition line: "Wide-ranging engagement, opportunity sensed at a distance". Keyword Reach, charge dynamic, poles catalyst Momentum / friction Scatter. Family function: Action. Cost dimension: opportunity sensed far off; the near things blur. Arena: horizon, wind, open road, far light, the next place. Classical portrait: wide-ranging engagement; opportunity sensed at a distance; windfall, generosity, the near things blur. Ruled domains: Opportunity, Ventures, Father. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 正财.
Element arena: Metal (edge, blade, ore, forge, whetstone, the clean line). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Fire. structural_interaction seed: "Fire directing Metal broadly — warmth applied to precision as distributed material".
- k2_overview: "Your Metal moves as the Horizon: an edge pointed outward. You mint opportunity, spotting value with an assayer’s eye and striking while metal is hot. Deals sharpen you, markets read like open books, and money is a tool you handle without trembling. Fortune favors your precision. Fence one treasury it cannot touch."
- k2_functional: "You strike opportunities with timing others envy: measured approach, decisive cut."
- adj_chips: {"friction":["Mercenary","Deal-hungry","Restless"],"catalyst":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Opportunity":"You see openings as clearly as flaws in ore: the undervalued asset, the mispriced moment. Trust the eye and audit the appetite. Two ventures cut deep beat ten scratched shallow.","Ventures":"Your ventures favor precision plays: quality arbitrage, timing trades, craft turned to commerce. Structure each like a blade, defined edge, clean handle, known length, and your record stays enviable.","Father":"The father-thread in your chart carries metal: a paternal figure of standards, trade, or discipline whose mark shows in how you value things. Settle those accounts. Honor or forgiveness both count as payment."}
- fn_reading.catalyst.ledger (three rows, index-aligned to adj_chips.catalyst; authored order is significance order):
  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 金_正财 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Thorough","Trustworthy","Slow and steady"],"friction":["No-frills","Greedy","Won’t budge"]}
- Sibling cell 金_正财 catalyst row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Detail is where your love of quality lives. The receipts reconciled monthly, the maintenance schedule honored, the small print actually read: your life runs on a fineness of attention that prevents disasters so early they never even become anecdotes. Nothing about you is approximately done."

Core element Fire, energy element Metal. Law: Fire tames Metal (火克金: the forge softens the blade). Relative to the core the energy is the tamed, so Metal is this core's Action. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Fire core that shows Metal on the catalyst pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The catalyst pole of Metal as the Action is the Overfueled band's case (the core has more than it channels); tone by pole: compliment. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 火_金's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: Before anyone else has looked up, you have spotted the opening. You stay awake on a far chance in view, and you spot the next one while you are claiming this one. You lose nothing by leaving one spotted opening untaken.

value_b.text: You spot openings before they open, and spotting is the pleasure. Since spotting first is how you feel safe, you put the far chance ahead of the near work. You pay with more openings spotted than finished, and one finish would settle that.

value.text: Spotting the opening comes easier than staying for it. You spot to feel ahead, and once the opening is yours you look out again rather than down into it. Take one spotted chance through to the money, since those you leave open close without you.

value.text: Whenever you spot an opening, you say so before knowing you want it. You spot out loud to share the excitement rather than plan. You spot far enough for two, and your partner loses only a week each time you point at something you skip.

value.text: Fast starts are your natural speed. You feel most alive in the first week, and this is why you start the next venture rather than sit through this one. Keep starting fast and give one start a middle, since you only get paid by staying.

value_b.text: You start fast, and often. You find the first move costs nothing and feels like proof, so you take a new start rather than a slow middle. Start half as often and you are still first, with a week left over for finishing.

value.text: Where you feel surest is starting fast. You start on speed alone, while you would rather spend your patience on a fresh start than a middle. Give the next middle the speed of its start, since you never get paid by what you keep restarting.

value.text: Starting fast means starting things for other people too. Since you start before your partner has agreed, you put your speed ahead of their say. You start early enough for both of you, and your partner misses only the chance to start it with you.

value.text: Giving freely is the first thing you do with what comes in. You feel money belongs to whoever needs it next, and you give it on rather than set it aside. Give as freely as you like and keep a share for yourself.

value_b.text: You give freely, and before anyone asks. You carry keeping as a weight and giving as a movement, so you hand things on sooner than you take them in. Give for as long as it feels like you, and keep back one thing.

value.text: Keeping is harder for you than giving freely. You would rather give money on than sit with it, since holding still feels like being stuck. Give yourself a share first, because you end up with nothing saved for the year you need it.

value.text: With the people around you, giving freely is how you stay close. You give often enough to be expected, and you give again rather than let that stand. You give enough for a family and leave the ones you love little chance to give back.
